sources.title: Language Models Represent Space and Time
sources.scope: Conference abstract reread in this round. Used as empirical prior art for prediction-trained language models containing world-related spatial/temporal representations.

sources.title: I Predict Therefore I Am: Is Next Token Prediction Enough to Learn Human-Interpretable Concepts from Data?
sources.scope: Conference abstract reread. Strong recent prior art for identifiability of latent discrete concepts under a generative next-token model.

sources.title: Toward Consistent World Models with Multi-Token Prediction and Latent Semantic Enhancement
sources.scope: ACL abstract and bibliographic record reread. Used as recent prior art for stronger internal belief-state pressure under multi-token prediction.

sources.title: Evaluating Self-Orienting in Language and Reasoning Models
sources.scope: Search-returned paper text/abstract inspected only; used as a nearby self/agent-orientation research lead, not as a basis for a detailed theorem or publication-status claim.

sources.title: Time, Identity and Consciousness in Language Model Agents
sources.scope: ArXiv abstract read. Relevant to separating stable-self talk from jointly instantiated identity organization; preprint, not treated as established validation of UCT.

novelty_status: Prediction-induced representation and self-orienting have strong prior art. R95 is a controlled project-specific acquisition/causal-use witness, not a historical-first theorem or AI-consciousness measurement.
